title.zh: 卷72 陽尼 賈思伯 李叔虎 路恃慶 房亮 曹世表 潘永基 朱元旭
title.en: Volume 72: Yang Ni, Jia Sibo, Li Shuhu, Lu Shiqing, Fang Liang, Cao Shibiao, Pan Yongji, Zhu Yuanxu
title.raw: 卷72 陽尼 賈思伯 李叔虎 路恃慶 房亮 曹世表 潘永基 朱元旭 Volume 72: Yang Ni, Jia Sibo, Li Shuhu, Lu Shiqing, Fang Liang, Cao Shibiao, Pan Yongji, Zhu Yuanxu

sentences.zh: 陽尼 賈思伯 李叔虎 路恃慶 房亮 曹世表 潘永基 朱元旭

translations.literal: Yang Ni, Jia Sibo, Li Shuhu, Lu Shiqing, Fang Liang, Cao Shibiao, Pan Yongji, Zhu Yuanxu
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ni, Jia Sibo, Li Shuhu, Lu Shiqing, Fang Liang, Cao Shibiao, Pan Yongji, and Zhu Yuanxu

sentences.zh: 陽尼，字景文，北平無終人。

translations.literal: Yang Ni, styled Jingwen, was a man of Wuzhong in Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ni, whose courtesy name was Jingwen, was a native of Wuzhong in Beiping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 少好學，博通羣籍，與上谷侯天護、頓丘李彪同志齊名。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning, thoroughly mastered all texts, and with Hou Tianhu of Shanggu and Li Biao of Dunqiu shared the same aspirations and equal fame.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he loved learning and mastered the full range of literature. Together with Hou Tianhu of Shanggu and Li Biao of Dunqiu he shared the same aspirations, and the three were equally renowned.

sentences.zh: 幽州刺史胡泥以尼學藝文雅，乃表薦之。

translations.literal: Youzhou Inspector Hu Ni, because Ni's learning and arts were refined and elegant, therefore memorialized recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ni, Inspector of Youzhou, recommended him by memorial on account of his refined scholarship and literary grace.

sentences.zh: 徵拜祕書著作郎，奏佛道宜在史錄。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Secretary in the Office of Compositions; he memorialized that Buddhism and Daoism should be recorded in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Secretary in the Office of Literary Composition, and submitted a memorial arguing that Buddhism and Daoism should be included in the historical records.

sentences.zh: 後改中書學為國子學，時中書監高閭、侍中李沖等以尼碩學博識，舉為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Later the Palace Library School was changed to the Imperial University. At that time Palace Library Supervisor Gao Li, Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Chong, and others, because Ni was deeply learned and broadly knowledgeable, recommended him as Chancellor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Palace Library School was reorganized as the Imperial University, Palace Library Supervisor Gao Li, Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Chong, and others recommended Ni for the post of Chancellor of the Imperial University in recognition of his profound erudition.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗親在苑堂講諸經典，詔尼侍聽，賜帛百匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu once personally lectured on the classics in the garden hall; he ordered Ni to attend and listen, and bestowed one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen once delivered lectures on the classics in person at the garden hall and ordered Ni to attend. He rewarded him with a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 尼後兼幽州中正。

translations.literal: Ni later concurrently served as Rectifier of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ni later also served concurrently as Rectifier of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 出為幽州平北府長史，帶漁陽太守，未拜，坐為中正時受鄉人財貨免官。

translations.literal: Sent out as Chief Clerk of the Pingbei Headquarters in Youzhou, concurrently holding the post of Administrator of Yuyang; before taking office, because while serving as Rectifier he received goods and money from a townsman, he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned Chief Clerk of the Pingbei Headquarters in Youzhou, with concurrent appointment as Administrator of Yuyang, but before he could take up the post he was dismissed from office for having accepted money and goods from a fellow townsman while serving as Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 尼每自傷曰：「吾昔未仕，不曾羨人，今日失官，與本何異？

translations.literal: Ni often lamented to himself, saying: "In the past when I had not yet taken office, I never envied others. Today I have lost office—how is this different from before?
translations.idiomatic: Ni often grieved aloud: "Before I entered service I never envied others. Now that I have lost my post, how is that any different from before?

sentences.zh: 然非吾宿志，命也如何！

translations.literal: Yet this was not my lifelong aim—what can one do against fate!
translations.idiomatic: Yet this was never my lifelong ambition. What can one do when fate wills otherwise?

sentences.zh: 」既而還鄉，遂卒於冀州，年六十一。

translations.literal: Afterwards he returned to his home district and died in Jizhou at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he returned to his native place and died in Jizhou at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 有書數千卷。

translations.literal: He possessed several thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: He left behind a library of several thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 所造字釋數十篇，未就而卒，其從孫太學博士承慶遂撰為字統二十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: The character glosses he composed numbered several tens of chapters; before completion he died. His grand-nephew the Erudite of the Imperial University Chengqing thereupon compiled them into twenty chapters entitled Zitong, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He had drafted several dozen chapters of character glosses but died before finishing the work. His grand-nephew Chengqing, an Erudite of the Imperial University, compiled them into the twenty-chapter Zitong, which then circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子介，字天佐。

translations.literal: His son Jie, styled Tianzuo.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jie, whose courtesy name was Tianzuo.

sentences.zh: 奉朝請，冀州默曹參軍。

translations.literal: Attendant at Court, Staff Officer in the Mo Bureau of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant at Court and as Staff Officer in the Mo Bureau of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 尼從子鳴鵠，鳴鵠弟季智，俱有名於時，前後並為幽州司馬。

translations.literal: Ni had grand-nephews Minghu and Minghu's younger brother Jizhi; both were famous in their time, and one after another both served as Commandant of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ni had grand-nephews Minghu and Jizhi, the latter Minghu's younger brother. Both were celebrated in their day, and each in turn served as Commandant of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 季智子璠，通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Jizhi's son Fan served as Regular Attendant of the Secretariat Through Direct Communications.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi's son Fan served as Regular Attendant of the Secretariat Through Direct Communications.

sentences.zh: 季智從弟荊，范陽太守，有吏能。

translations.literal: Jizhi's younger cousin Jing was Administrator of Fanyang and possessed administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi's younger cousin Jing served as Administrator of Fanyang and was known for his administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平西將軍、東益州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Eastern Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Eastern Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 季智從子伯慶，汝南太守。

translations.literal: Jizhi's grand-nephew Boqing was Administrator of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi's grand-nephew Boqing served as Administrator of Runan.

sentences.zh: 伯慶從父弟藻，字景德。

translations.literal: Boqing's younger paternal cousin Zao, styled Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: Boqing's younger paternal cousin Zao, whose courtesy name was Jingde.

sentences.zh: 少孤，有雅志，涉獵經史。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he had refined aspirations and broadly read the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he cherished refined ambitions and read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 太和初，舉秀才，射策高第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe era he was nominated as Cultivated Talent and ranked highest in the archery examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taihe era he was recommended as a cultivated talent and placed at the top of the archery examination.

sentences.zh: 以母疾還。

translations.literal: Because his mother was ill he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home when his mother fell ill.

sentences.zh: 徵拜中書博士，詔兼禮官，拜燕宣王廟於長安。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Erudite of the Palace Secretariat; ordered concurrently to serve as ceremonial officer and perform rites at the temple of Prince Xuan of Yan in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Erudite of the Palace Secretariat, then ordered to serve concurrently as a ceremonial officer and perform rites at the temple of Prince Xuan of Yan in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 還，授寧遠將軍，賜爵魏昌男。

translations.literal: On his return he was granted the title General Who Establishes Distant Regions and enfeoffed as Baron of Weichang.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed General Who Establishes Distant Regions and enfeoffed as Baron of Weichang.

sentences.zh: 選為廷尉正，轉考功郎中。

translations.literal: Selected as Director under the Minister of Justice, then transferred to Aide in the Bureau of Merit Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as Director under the Minister of Justice and later transferred to Aide in the Bureau of Merit Evaluation.

sentences.zh: 除建德太守。

translations.literal: Appointed Administrator of Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Jiande.

sentences.zh: 以清貧，賜帛六十匹。

translations.literal: Because of his integrity and poverty, he was granted sixty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his integrity and poverty, the court granted him sixty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 尋假寧遠將軍，領統軍，外防內撫，甚得居邊之稱。

translations.literal: Soon he was temporarily made General Who Establishes Distant Regions and placed in command of a garrison army; he defended the frontier abroad and soothed the people within, winning great renown as a border administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was temporarily appointed General Who Establishes Distant Regions and placed in command of a garrison army. He defended the frontier and soothed the people within, winning wide renown as a border administrator.

sentences.zh: 解任還家，久之，除兗州左將軍府長史，又拜瀛州安東府長史，加揚烈將軍。

translations.literal: Relieved of office and returned home; after a long while appointed Chief Clerk of the Left General's Headquarters in Yanzhou, then Chief Clerk of the Andong Headquarters in Yingzhou, with the additional title General Who Displays Firmness.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office and returning home, he was later appointed Chief Clerk of the Left General's Headquarters in Yanzhou, then Chief Clerk of the Andong Headquarters in Yingzhou, with the additional title General Who Displays Firmness.

sentences.zh: 藻以年老歸家，闔門不關世事。

translations.literal: When Zao grew old he retired home; his entire household paid no heed to worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zao grew old he retired home, and his entire household ceased to concern itself with worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，在鄉為賊帥杜洛周所囚，發病卒。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era, while at home in the countryside he was imprisoned by the bandit chief Du Luozhou, fell ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era, while at home in the countryside he was imprisoned by the bandit chief Du Luozhou, fell ill, and died.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，贈征虜將軍、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he was posthumously appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era he was posthumously appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 子貞，字世幹。

translations.literal: His son Zhen, styled Shigan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen, whose courtesy name was Shigan.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 貞弟弼，字世輔。

translations.literal: Zhen's younger brother Bi, styled Shifu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's younger brother Bi, whose courtesy name was Shifu.

sentences.zh: 長於吏事。

translations.literal: He excelled at administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 本州別駕，加輕車將軍。

translations.literal: Vice-Prefect of his home province, with the additional title General of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice-Prefect of his home province, with the additional title General of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 屬洛周陷城，弼遂率宗親南渡河，居於青州。

translations.literal: When Luozhou captured the city, Bi thereupon led his clansmen south across the Yellow River and settled in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Luozhou captured the city, Bi led his clansmen south across the Yellow River and settled in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 值邢杲起逆，青州城民疑河北人為杲內應，遂害弼，時年四十八。

translations.literal: When Xing Guo rose in rebellion, the people of Qingzhou city suspected that northerners were Guo's secret allies inside the walls, and so killed Bi. He was forty-eight at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing Guo rose in rebellion, the people of Qingzhou suspected that northerners were Guo's secret allies within the city and killed Bi. He was forty-eight at the time.

sentences.zh: 子撝，襲祖爵。

translations.literal: His son Hui inherited his grandfather's noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui inherited his grandfather's noble rank.

sentences.zh: 弼弟斐，武定末，尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Bi's younger brother Fei, at the end of the Wuding era, served as Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's younger brother Fei served as Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of Works at the end of the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 藻從弟令鮮，京兆王愉郎中令。

translations.literal: Zao's younger cousin Lingxian served as Director of the Palace Domestic Service under the Prince of Jingzhao, Yuan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Zao's younger cousin Lingxian served as Director of the Palace Domestic Service under the Prince of Jingzhao, Yuan Yu.

sentences.zh: 坐同愉反，逃竄免。

translations.literal: Implicated in Yu's rebellion, he fled into hiding and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in Yu's rebellion, he fled into hiding and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 會赦，除名。

translations.literal: An amnesty was granted, and he was struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty was granted, he was struck from the registers.

sentences.zh: 子世和，武定末，齊州驃騎司馬。

translations.literal: His son Shihe, at the end of the Wuding era, served as Commandant of the Rapid Cavalry Staff in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shihe served as Commandant of the Rapid Cavalry Staff in Qizhou at the end of the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 藻從弟延興，南豳州刺史。

translations.literal: Zao's younger cousin Yanxing was Inspector of Southern Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zao's younger cousin Yanxing served as Inspector of Southern Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 延興從弟固，字敬安。

translations.literal: Yanxing's younger cousin Gu, styled Jing'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxing's younger cousin Gu, whose courtesy name was Jing'an.

sentences.zh: 性俶儻，不拘小節，少任俠，好劍客，弗事生產。

translations.literal: By nature bold and free-spirited, heedless of small proprieties; in youth he acted the knight-errant, loved swordsmen, and did not engage in productive work.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was bold and free-spirited, heedless of small proprieties. In youth he played the knight-errant, consorted with swordsmen, and would not engage in honest livelihood.

sentences.zh: 年二十六，始折節好學，遂博覽篇籍，有文才。

translations.literal: At twenty-six he at last restrained himself and turned to study, then read widely in texts and possessed literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-six he at last reined himself in and turned to study, then read widely in the literature and showed real literary talent.

sentences.zh: 太和中，從大將軍宋王劉昶征義陽，板府法曹行參軍，假陵江將軍。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he followed the Great General, Prince of Song Liu Chang, on the campaign against Yiyang; appointed provisional Acting Staff Officer in the Law Bureau of the headquarters, with the temporary title General Who Crosses the River.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he followed the Great General, Prince of Song Liu Chang, on the campaign against Yiyang. He was appointed provisional Acting Staff Officer in the headquarters Law Bureau, with the temporary title General Who Crosses the River.

sentences.zh: 昶嚴暴，治軍甚急，三軍戰慄無敢言者。

translations.literal: Chang was severe and brutal and governed the army with extreme harshness; the entire army trembled with fear and no one dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was severe and brutal and ran the army with extreme harshness. The whole army trembled with fear, and no one dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 固啟諫，并面陳事宜。

translations.literal: Gu submitted a remonstrance and also stated his views face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Gu submitted a written remonstrance and also stated his views to Chang in person.

sentences.zh: 昶大怒，欲斬之，使監當攻道。

translations.literal: Chang flew into a rage and wanted to execute him, but instead made him supervise the assault route.
translations.idiomatic: Chang flew into a rage and wanted to execute him, but instead assigned him to supervise the assault route.

sentences.zh: 固在軍勇決，志意閑雅，了無懼色。

translations.literal: Gu in the army was bold and resolute; his bearing was calm and elegant, and he showed not the slightest fear.
translations.idiomatic: In the field Gu was bold and resolute, calm and dignified in bearing, and showed not the slightest fear.

sentences.zh: 昶甚奇之。

translations.literal: Chang was greatly impressed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was greatly impressed by him.

sentences.zh: 軍還，言之高祖。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he reported this to Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he reported this to Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 年三十餘，始辟大將軍府參軍事，署城局，仍從昶鎮彭城，板兼長史。

translations.literal: In his thirties he was first recruited as staff officer in a general's headquarters, assigned to the city bureau; he then followed Chang to garrison Pengcheng and was appointed provisional concurrent Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In his thirties he was first recruited as a staff officer in a general's headquarters and assigned to the city bureau. He then followed Chang to garrison Pengcheng and was appointed provisional concurrent Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 俄以憂去任。

translations.literal: Soon he left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 裴叔業以淮南內附，世宗詔平南將軍、廣陵侯元衎與司徒、彭城王勰同鎮壽春，敕固為衎司馬。

translations.literal: When Pei Shuye brought Huainan over to Wei, Emperor Shizong ordered General Who Pacifies the South, Marquis of Guangling Yuan Kan, together with the Minister of Works, Prince of Pengcheng Xie, to garrison Shouchun jointly; Gu was ordered to serve as Kan's marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Shuye brought Huainan over to Wei, Emperor Xuanwu ordered General Who Pacifies the South, Marquis of Guangling Yuan Kan, together with the Minister of Works, Prince of Pengcheng Xie, to garrison Shouchun jointly, and appointed Gu as Kan's marshal.

sentences.zh: 還，除太尉西閤祭酒，兼廷尉評。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Libationer in the Western Pavilion of the Grand Marshal, concurrently serving as Examiner under the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Libationer in the Western Pavilion of the Grand Marshal and concurrently served as Examiner under the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 上改定律令議。

translations.literal: He submitted opinions on revising the statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted opinions on revising the statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 除給事中。

translations.literal: Appointed Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出為試守北平太守，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: Sent out as provisional Administrator of Beiping; his benevolent governance was notable.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as provisional Administrator of Beiping and governed with notable benevolence.

sentences.zh: 久之，以公事免。

translations.literal: After a long while he was dismissed on account of official business.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was dismissed on account of official business.

sentences.zh: 後除給事中，領侍御史。

translations.literal: Later appointed Gentleman Attendant and placed in charge of the Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Gentleman Attendant and placed in charge of the Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 轉治書，劾奏廣平王懷、汝南王悅、南陽長公主。

translations.literal: Transferred to Drafting Secretary; he impeached Prince of Guangping Huai, Prince of Runan Yue, and the Princess of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to drafting secretary and impeached Prince Huai of Guangping, Prince Yue of Runan, and the Princess of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 及使懷荒，鎮將萬貳望風逃走。

translations.literal: When Huai was sent to the frontier, the garrison commander Wan Er fled at the first report of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai was sent to govern the frontier, the garrison commander Wan Er fled at the first sign of trouble.

sentences.zh: 劾恒農太守裴粲免官。

translations.literal: He impeached Pei Can, Administrator of Hengnong, who was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Pei Can, Administrator of Hengnong, who was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 時世宗廣訪得失，固上讜言表曰：「臣聞為治不在多方，在於力行而已。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Shizong broadly sought opinions on strengths and weaknesses; Gu submitted a straightforward memorial stating: "Your subject has heard that governing does not depend on many expedients, but on earnest execution alone.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xuanwu broadly sought opinions on the strengths and failings of government. Gu submitted a straightforward memorial stating: "Your subject has heard that governing does not depend on many expedients, but on earnest execution alone.

sentences.zh: 當今之務，宜早正東儲，立師傅以保護，立官司以防衞，以係蒼生之心；

translations.literal: The urgent task of the present is to establish the Eastern Heir Apparent early, appoint tutors to protect him, establish offices to guard him, and thereby bind the hearts of the common people;
translations.idiomatic: The urgent task of the present is to establish the Eastern Heir Apparent early, appoint tutors to protect him, establish offices to guard him, and thereby win the hearts of the people;

sentences.zh: 攬權衡，親宗室，強幹弱枝，以立萬世之計；

translations.literal: hold the scales of power, draw close the imperial clan, strengthen the trunk and weaken the branches, and thereby establish a plan for ten thousand generations;
translations.idiomatic: hold the scales of power, draw the imperial clan close, strengthen the trunk and weaken the branches, and thereby lay a plan for ten thousand generations;

sentences.zh: 舉賢良，黜不肖，使野無遺才，朝無素餐；

translations.literal: promote the worthy and dismiss the unfit, so that in the wilds no talent is overlooked and at court no one eats idle salaries;
translations.idiomatic: promote the worthy and dismiss the unfit, so that in the wilds no talent is overlooked and at court no one eats idle salaries;

sentences.zh: 孜孜萬幾，躬勤庶務，使民無謗讟之響；

translations.literal: attend diligently to the myriad affairs of state and personally labor at everyday administration, so that the people utter no sounds of slander and complaint;
translations.idiomatic: attend diligently to the myriad affairs of state and personally labor at everyday administration, so that the people utter no sounds of slander and complaint;

sentences.zh: 省徭役，薄賦斂；

translations.literal: reduce corvée labor and lighten taxes and levies;
translations.idiomatic: reduce corvée labor and lighten taxes and levies;

sentences.zh: 修學官，遵舊章；

translations.literal: restore the schools and follow the old regulations;
translations.idiomatic: restore the schools and follow the old regulations;

sentences.zh: 貴農桑，賤工賈；

translations.literal: honor agriculture and sericulture and hold craftsmen and merchants in low esteem;
translations.idiomatic: honor agriculture and sericulture and hold craftsmen and merchants in low esteem;

sentences.zh: 絕談虛窮微之論，簡桑門無用之費。

translations.literal: cut off empty talk of abstruse metaphysics and reduce the useless expenditures on Buddhist monks.
translations.idiomatic: cut off empty talk of abstruse metaphysics and reduce the useless expenditures on Buddhist monks.

sentences.zh: 以存元元之民，以救飢寒之苦，上合昊天之心，下悅億兆之望。

translations.literal: Thus preserve the common people, relieve the suffering of hunger and cold, align with the heart of Heaven above, and satisfy the hopes of the hundred million below.
translations.idiomatic: Thus preserve the common people, relieve the suffering of hunger and cold, align with the heart of Heaven above, and satisfy the hopes of the hundred million below.

sentences.zh: 然後備器械，修甲兵，習水戰，滅吳會，撰封禪之禮，襲軒唐之軌，同彼七十二君之徽號，協定鼎嵩河之心，副高祖殷勤之寄。

translations.literal: Only then prepare weapons and equipment, repair armor and arms, practice naval warfare, destroy Wu and Kuaiji, compose the rites of the feng and shan sacrifices, follow the tracks of Xuanyuan and Tang, match the august titles of those seventy-two sage rulers, harmonize with the resolve to fix the tripod at Mount Song and the river, and fulfill the earnest charge of Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Only then prepare weapons and equipment, repair armor and arms, practice naval warfare, destroy Wu and Kuaiji, compose the rites of the feng and shan sacrifices, follow the tracks of Xuanyuan and Tang, match the august titles of those seventy-two sage rulers, harmonize with the resolve to fix the tripod at Mount Song and the river, and fulfill the earnest charge of Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 上與三皇比隆，下與五帝齊美。

translations.literal: Above you would rank with the Three Sovereigns in splendor; below you would match the Five Emperors in glory.
translations.idiomatic: Above you would rank with the Three Sovereigns in splendor; below you would match the Five Emperors in glory.

sentences.zh: 豈不茂哉！

translations.literal: Would this not be glorious!
translations.idiomatic: Would this not be glorious!

sentences.zh: 臣位卑識昧，言不及義，屬聖明廣訪，敢獻瞽言。

translations.literal: Your subject's rank is low and understanding dim; my words fall short of what is right. Since the sage ruler broadly seeks counsel, I dare offer blind counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject's rank is low and understanding dim, and my words fall short of what is right. Since Your Majesty broadly seeks counsel, I dare offer this blind counsel.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下留神，少垂究察。」

translations.literal: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will give attention and bestow a little investigation and scrutiny."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will give the matter attention and bestow a little investigation and scrutiny."

sentences.zh: 初，世宗委任羣下，不甚親覽，好桑門之法。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Shizong delegated affairs to his subordinates and did not much attend to matters personally; he favored the Buddhist teaching.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Xuanwu delegated affairs to his subordinates and did not much attend to matters personally; he favored the Buddhist teaching.

sentences.zh: 尚書令高肇以外戚權寵，專決朝事；

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Zhao, as a maternal relative enjoying power and favor, monopolized decisions in court affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, Director of the Masters of Writing, as a maternal relative enjoying power and favor, monopolized decisions in court affairs;

sentences.zh: 又咸陽王禧等並有釁故，宗室大臣，相見疏薄；

translations.literal: Moreover Prince of Xianyang Xi and others all had causes for offense; among the imperial clan and great ministers, mutual regard grew thin;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Prince Xi of Xianyang and others all had causes for offense, and among the imperial clan and great ministers mutual regard grew thin;

sentences.zh: 而王畿民庶，勞弊益甚。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the people of the capital region grew ever more worn and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the people of the capital region grew ever more worn and exhausted.

sentences.zh: 固乃作南、北二都賦，稱恒代田漁聲樂侈靡之事，節以中京禮儀之式，因以諷諫。

translations.literal: Gu thereupon composed the Rhapsodies on the Southern and Northern Capitals, describing the field sports, fishing, music, and extravagant affairs of Heng and Dai, restrained by the ritual forms of the Central Capital, and thereby offered indirect admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Gu thereupon composed the Rhapsodies on the Southern and Northern Capitals, describing the field sports, fishing, music, and extravagant affairs of Heng and Dai, counterpointed by the ritual forms of the Central Capital, and thereby offered indirect admonition.

sentences.zh: 辭多不載。

translations.literal: Most of the text is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the text is not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 世宗末，中尉王顯起宅既成，集僚屬饗宴。

translations.literal: Near the end of Emperor Shizong's reign, Chief Commandant Wang Xian, having finished building his residence, gathered his subordinates for a feast.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Xuanwu's reign, Chief Commandant Wang Xian, having finished building his residence, gathered his subordinates for a feast.

sentences.zh: 酒酣問固曰：「此宅何如？

translations.literal: When the wine had gone deep he asked Gu: "What do you think of this residence?
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had gone deep he asked Gu: "What do you think of this residence?

sentences.zh: 」固對曰：「晏嬰湫隘，流稱于今；

translations.literal: Gu replied: "Yan Ying's narrow dwelling has been celebrated to this day;
translations.idiomatic: Gu replied: "Yan Ying's narrow dwelling has been celebrated to this day;

sentences.zh: 豐屋生災，著於周易。

translations.literal: lavish houses bring disaster, as recorded in the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: lavish houses bring disaster, as recorded in the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 此蓋同傳舍耳，唯有德能卒。

translations.literal: This is merely like a relay station; only virtue can see one through to the end.
translations.idiomatic: This is merely like a relay station; only virtue can see one through to the end.

sentences.zh: 願公勉之。

translations.literal: I hope you will exert yourself in this.
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will exert yourself in this.

sentences.zh: 」顯默然。

translations.literal: Xian fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Xian fell silent.

sentences.zh: 他日又謂固曰：「吾作太府卿，庫藏充實，卿以為何如？

translations.literal: Another day he again said to Gu: "When I served as Minister of the Grand Treasury, the storehouses were full and abundant—what do you think of that?
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he again said to Gu: "When I served as Minister of the Grand Treasury, the treasuries were stocked to overflowing—what do you think of that?

sentences.zh: 」固對曰：「公收百官之祿四分之一，州郡贓贖悉入京藏，以此充府，未足為多。

translations.literal: Gu replied: "Your Lordship took one-fourth of all officials' salaries; bribes and ransom payments from the provinces and commanderies all went into the capital treasuries—using these to fill the storehouses is hardly a great amount.
translations.idiomatic: Gu replied: "Your Lordship took one-fourth of every official's salary; all bribes and fines from the provinces and commanderies went straight into the capital coffers. To fill your storehouses from such sources is hardly much to boast of.

sentences.zh: 且有聚斂之臣，寧有盜臣，豈不戒哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, there are ministers who gather wealth—are there ever ministers who steal? Should one not take warning!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, a minister who amasses wealth may well be called a thief. Should one not take warning from that!

sentences.zh: 」顯大不悅，以此銜固。

translations.literal: Xian was greatly displeased and on this account bore a grudge against Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was deeply offended and from then on harbored a grudge against Gu.

sentences.zh: 又有人間固於顯，顯因奏固剩請米麥，免固官。

translations.literal: Moreover someone slandered Gu to Xian; Xian thereupon memorialized that Gu had fraudulently requisitioned grain, and removed Gu from office.
translations.idiomatic: Someone also slandered Gu to Xian. Xian thereupon memorialized that Gu had fraudulently requisitioned grain and grain, and had him dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 既無事役，遂闔門自守，著演賾賦，以明幽微通塞之事。

translations.literal: With no official duties, he thereupon shut his doors and kept to himself, composing the Rhapsody on the Unfolding of the Hidden to clarify matters of obscurity and clarity, blockage and passage.
translations.idiomatic: With no official duties left to him, he shut his doors and kept to himself, composing the Rhapsody on the Unfolding of the Hidden to set forth how what is hidden and what is manifest, blocked and open, turn upon one another.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：

translations.literal: Its words read:
translations.idiomatic: Its words read:

sentences.zh: 紹有周之遐軌兮，初錫世於河陽。

translations.literal: Continuing the distant tracks of Zhou, first granted a fief at Heyang—
translations.idiomatic: We followed the far road of Zhou, first granted a fief at Heyang—

sentences.zh: 建甸侯而列爵兮，與王室而並昌。

translations.literal: establishing the Marquisate of Dian and receiving rank, flourishing together with the royal house—
translations.idiomatic: raised up as Marquis of Dian and enfeoffed with rank, flourishing side by side with the royal house—

sentences.zh: 遭季葉之紛亂兮，仍矯迹於良鄉。

translations.literal: meeting the disorder of the late age, still traced our path at Liangxiang—
translations.idiomatic: then, in the chaos of the dynasty's decline, still traced our path at Liangxiang—

sentences.zh: 棄侯衞之楨弼兮，乃殖根於幽方。

translations.literal: abandoning the pillar-support of Hou Wei, took root in the northern region—
translations.idiomatic: leaving behind the pillar-support of Hou and Wei, we took root in the northern lands—

sentences.zh: 自祖考而輝烈兮，逮余躬而翳微。

translations.literal: from ancestors and forefathers shining in glory, down to my own person dim and slight—
translations.idiomatic: from ancestors blazing in glory down to my own person, dim and slight—

sentences.zh: 懼堂構之頹撓兮，恐崩毀其洪基。

translations.literal: fearing the hall's framework would collapse and totter, dreading the ruin of its great foundation—
translations.idiomatic: I fear the hall's frame may topple and totter; I dread the ruin of its great foundation—

sentences.zh: 心惴惴而慄慄兮，若臨深而履薄。

translations.literal: my heart anxious and trembling, as if facing a deep abyss and treading on thin ice—
translations.idiomatic: my heart anxious and trembling, as if standing over a deep abyss on thin ice—

sentences.zh: 登喬木而長吟兮，抗幽谷而靡託。

translations.literal: climbing a tall tree to chant long, standing against a dark valley with nowhere to rest—
translations.idiomatic: I climb a tall tree and chant long; I stand against a dark valley with nowhere to rest—

sentences.zh: 何身輕而任重兮，懼顛墜於峻壑。

translations.literal: how can the body be slight yet the burden heavy— I fear tumbling into a steep ravine—
translations.idiomatic: how can one so slight bear so heavy a burden? I fear tumbling into a steep ravine—

sentences.zh: 憑神明之扶助兮，雖幽微而獲存。

translations.literal: relying on the divine powers' support, though obscure and slight yet preserved—
translations.idiomatic: supported by the divine powers, though obscure and slight we yet survive—

sentences.zh: 賴先后之醇德兮，乃保護其遺孫。

translations.literal: trusting in the pure virtue of forebears, they protect their surviving descendants—
translations.idiomatic: trusting in the pure virtue of our forebears, they protect their surviving descendants—

sentences.zh: 伊日月之屢遷兮，何四時之相逼。

translations.literal: Ah, sun and moon shift again and again— how the four seasons press upon one another—
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon shift again and again; how the four seasons press upon one another—

sentences.zh: 知年命之有期兮，慨斡流之不息。

translations.literal: knowing that life's span has its term, sighing that the turning stream never ceases—
translations.idiomatic: knowing that life's span has its term, I sigh that the turning stream never ceases—

sentences.zh: 傷艱躓之相承兮，悲屯蹇而日臻。

translations.literal: grieving that hardship and stumbling follow in succession, sorrowing that obstruction and difficulty draw nearer day by day—
translations.idiomatic: I grieve that hardship and stumbling follow in succession; I sorrow that obstruction and difficulty draw nearer day by day—

sentences.zh: 心惻愴而不懌兮，乃有懷於古人。

translations.literal: my heart grieved and not at ease, therefore I turn my thoughts to the ancients—
translations.idiomatic: my heart grieved and ill at ease, I turn my thoughts to the ancients—

sentences.zh: 或垂綸於渭濱兮，有胥靡於傅巖。

translations.literal: some cast their lines on the Wei shore; some were convict laborers at Fuyan—
translations.idiomatic: some cast their lines on the Wei shore; some were convict laborers at Fuyan—

sentences.zh: 既應繇而赴兆兮，作殷周之元鑒。

translations.literal: having answered the oracle and gone to the omen, they became the primal mirror of Yin and Zhou—
translations.idiomatic: having answered the oracle and gone to meet their destiny, they became the primal mirror of Yin and Zhou—

sentences.zh: 孔栖栖而不息兮，終見黜於庶邦。

translations.literal: Confucius restless and never at rest, in the end was dismissed among the common states—
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, restless and never at rest, in the end was cast out among the common states—

sentences.zh: 墨馳騁而不已兮，亦舉世而不容。

translations.literal: Mo Di galloped on without cease, yet the whole world would not accept him—
translations.idiomatic: Mo Di galloped on without cease, yet the whole world would not accept him—

sentences.zh: 有鸞孤而爭國兮，有讓位而採薇。

translations.literal: some, like the lone phoenix, fought for the realm; some yielded the throne and gathered wild greens—
translations.idiomatic: some, like the lone phoenix, fought for the realm; some yielded the throne and gathered wild greens—

sentences.zh: 有躍馬而赴會兮，有棲遲以俟時。

translations.literal: some leapt on horseback to keep their rendezvous; some lingered and waited for the right time—
translations.idiomatic: some leapt on horseback to keep their rendezvous; some lingered and waited for the right moment—

sentences.zh: 曹納辛而袁亡兮，袁戮田而曹盛。

translations.literal: Cao took in Xin and Yuan perished; Yuan killed Tian and Cao flourished—
translations.idiomatic: Cao took in Xin and Yuan perished; Yuan killed Tian and Cao flourished—

sentences.zh: 鮑授州而得時兮，韓棄牧而失性。

translations.literal: Bao received a province and caught the moment; Han abandoned his fief and lost his nature—
translations.idiomatic: Bao received a province and caught the moment; Han abandoned his fief and lost his true self—

sentences.zh: 趙堯門而誕聖兮，終夭隱而不繁。

translations.literal: from the gate of Zhao Yao a sage was born, yet in the end died young and obscure without posterity—
translations.idiomatic: from the gate of Zhao Yao a sage was born, yet in the end died young and obscure, leaving no posterity—

sentences.zh: 衞泯軀於世難兮，啟洪業於宣元。

translations.literal: Wei lost his body in worldly calamity, yet opened a great enterprise in the Xuanyuan era—
translations.idiomatic: Wei lost his life in worldly calamity, yet opened a great enterprise in the Xuanyuan era—

sentences.zh: 釋臯繇之法憲兮，見蓼六之先亡。

translations.literal: abandoning Gao Yao's laws and statutes, one saw the six states of Liao perish first—
translations.idiomatic: when Gao Yao's laws and statutes were cast aside, the six states of Liao were the first to perish—

sentences.zh: 練疑枉於怨獄兮，寧于公之獨昌。

translations.literal: Lian Ying was wronged in a prison born of hatred; only Lord Ning alone flourished—
translations.idiomatic: Lian Ying was wronged in a prison born of hatred; only Lord Ning alone flourished—

sentences.zh: 明禍福之同門兮，知休咎之異塗。

translations.literal: understanding that fortune and misfortune share one gate, knowing that weal and woe take different roads—
translations.idiomatic: I see that fortune and misfortune share one gate, yet weal and woe take different roads—

sentences.zh: 尋倚伏之無源兮，或先詘而後舒。

translations.literal: seeking the sourceless alternation of decline and rise, sometimes first bent low and later extended—
translations.idiomatic: seeking the sourceless alternation of decline and rise, sometimes one is first bent low and later extended—

sentences.zh: 賜憑軒而策駟兮，撫清琴而自娛。

translations.literal: Zi-gong leaned on the railing and drove four horses, stroking a clear zither to amuse himself—
translations.idiomatic: Zi-gong leaned on the railing and drove four horses, stroking a clear zither to amuse himself—

sentences.zh: 憲服弊於陋巷兮，蘊六藝於蓬廬。

translations.literal: Yuan Xian wore rags in a mean alley, storing the Six Arts in a thatched hut—
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian wore rags in a mean alley, storing the Six Arts in a thatched hut—

sentences.zh: 勃計行而致位兮，錯謀合而身傾。

translations.literal: Bo Ji planned his course and reached high rank; Chao Cuo's plans succeeded yet his person was overturned—
translations.idiomatic: Bo Ji planned his course and reached high rank; Chao Cuo's plans succeeded yet his person was overturned—

sentences.zh: 蕭功成而福集兮，韓勳立而禍并。

translations.literal: Xiao He achieved merit and blessings gathered; Han Xin stood in merit yet calamity came with it—
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He achieved merit and blessings gathered; Han Xin stood in merit yet calamity came with it—

sentences.zh: 紛回平而綿結兮，亮未識其幽情。

translations.literal: tangled and level, continuous and knotted— clearly I have not yet grasped their hidden truth—
translations.idiomatic: tangled and level, continuous and knotted— clearly I have not yet grasped their hidden truth—

sentences.zh: 有積毀而恩昵兮，有積譽而寵衰。

translations.literal: some accumulate slander yet remain in favor; some accumulate praise yet see favor fade—
translations.idiomatic: some accumulate slander yet remain in favor; some accumulate praise yet see favor fade—

sentences.zh: 或形乖而意合兮，或身密而志離。

translations.literal: some are at odds in form yet united in intent; some are close in body yet parted in will—
translations.idiomatic: some are at odds in form yet united in intent; some are close in body yet parted in will—

sentences.zh: 情與貌而紛競兮，體與識而交馳。

translations.literal: feeling and appearance contend in confusion; body and understanding race against each other—
translations.idiomatic: feeling and appearance contend in confusion; body and understanding race against each other—

sentences.zh: 旦流言而見疑，先緣謗而益信。

translations.literal: Dan was slandered and came under suspicion; Xian was first slandered yet grew more trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was slandered and came under suspicion; Xian was first slandered yet grew more trusted.

sentences.zh: 樂食子而中疏兮，巴放麑而日進。

translations.literal: Yue Ying's son was eaten and he grew estranged at heart; Ba released the fawn and advanced day by day—
translations.idiomatic: Yue Ying's son was eaten and he grew estranged at heart; Ba released the fawn and advanced day by day—

sentences.zh: 或舉世而稱賢兮，偶不合於主心。

translations.literal: some are praised by the whole world, yet happen not to accord with their lord's heart—
translations.idiomatic: some are praised by the whole world, yet happen not to accord with their lord's heart—

sentences.zh: 或居鄉而三黜兮，獨為時之所欽。

translations.literal: some dwell in their home district and are thrice dismissed, yet alone are admired by the age—
translations.idiomatic: some dwell in their home district and are thrice dismissed, yet alone are admired by the age—

sentences.zh: 或負鼎而干主兮，或杖策於幽林。

translations.literal: some carry a cauldron to seek audience with their lord; some lean on a staff in a dark forest—
translations.idiomatic: some carry a cauldron to seek audience with their lord; some lean on a staff in a dark forest—

sentences.zh: 或望旗而色阻兮，或臨危而撫琴。

translations.literal: some see the banner and their color changes with fear; some face peril and stroke the zither—
translations.idiomatic: some see the banner and their color changes with fear; some face peril and stroke the zither—

sentences.zh: 道有大而由小兮，義有顯而必微。

translations.literal: the Way has what is great yet proceeds from what is small; righteousness has what is manifest yet must be subtle—
translations.idiomatic: the Way has what is great yet proceeds from what is small; righteousness has what is manifest yet must be subtle—

sentences.zh: 理貴在於得要兮，事終成於會機。

translations.literal: in principle what is prized is grasping the essential; affairs in the end succeed through meeting the right moment—
translations.idiomatic: in principle what is prized is grasping the essential; affairs in the end succeed through meeting the right moment—

sentences.zh: 每一日而三省兮，亦有念而九思。

translations.literal: each day thrice examining oneself— there is also reflection with ninefold thought—
translations.idiomatic: each day thrice examining oneself— there is also reflection with ninefold thought—

sentences.zh: 孰有是而可是兮，孰有非而可非。

translations.literal: who has what is right that can be affirmed as right? who has what is wrong that can be condemned as wrong?
translations.idiomatic: who has what is right that can be affirmed as right? who has what is wrong that can be condemned as wrong?

sentences.zh: 石育子而啟夏兮，鳦遺卵而孕殷。

translations.literal: A stone bore a child and opened the Xia; the swallow left an egg and conceived the Yin—
translations.idiomatic: A stone bore a child and opened the Xia; the swallow left an egg and conceived the Yin—

sentences.zh: 鳥藉冰而存棄兮，虎乳孩以字文。

translations.literal: a bird relied on ice to survive yet was abandoned; a tiger nursed an infant and gave him the surname Wen—
translations.idiomatic: a bird relied on ice to survive yet was abandoned; a tiger nursed an infant and gave him the surname Wen—

sentences.zh: 發昇舟而魚躍兮，季潛軀而覆雲。

translations.literal: Fa ascended a boat and fish leapt; Ji hid his body and overturned the clouds—
translations.idiomatic: Fa ascended a boat and fish leapt; Ji hid his body and overturned the clouds—

sentences.zh: 或揮戈而爭帝兮，或洗耳而辭君。

translations.literal: some waved spears and fought for the throne; some washed their ears and declined their lord—
translations.idiomatic: some waved spears and fought for the throne; some washed their ears and declined their lord—

sentences.zh: 道曲成而不一兮，神參差而異兆。

translations.literal: the Way completes itself in curves and is not one; the divine is uneven and gives different omens—
translations.idiomatic: the Way completes itself in curves and is not one; the divine is uneven and gives different omens—

sentences.zh: 茲聖達之未明兮，豈前修之克了。

translations.literal: if even sages and the enlightened have not understood this, how could earlier worthies fully grasp it?
translations.idiomatic: if even sages and the enlightened have not understood this, how could earlier worthies fully grasp it?

sentences.zh: 迷白日之近遙兮，方有闚於天表。

translations.literal: Mistaking the white sun's nearness and distance, just now I have glimpsed heaven's outer rim—
translations.idiomatic: Mistaking the white sun's nearness and distance, just now I have glimpsed heaven's outer rim—

sentences.zh: 且臨海而觀瀾兮，何津源之杳杳。

translations.literal: and now facing the sea and watching the waves— how distant and dim the ford's source—
translations.idiomatic: and now facing the sea and watching the waves— how distant and dim the ford's source—

sentences.zh: 文遷繹而身徂兮，景守節而災移。

translations.literal: King Wen moved his capital and his person departed; King Jing kept his integrity and calamity shifted—
translations.idiomatic: King Wen moved his capital and his person departed; King Jing kept his integrity and calamity shifted—

sentences.zh: 湯改祝而革命兮，靈投策而詬龜。

translations.literal: Tang changed the sacrificial prayer and transformed the mandate; Ling cast the stalks and reviled the tortoise—
translations.idiomatic: Tang changed the sacrificial prayer and transformed the mandate; Ling cast the stalks and reviled the tortoise—

sentences.zh: 圉據胎而為巨兮，友發文而自相。

translations.literal: Yu held the fetus and became a giant; You Fa raised an army and turned against himself—
translations.idiomatic: Yu held the fetus and became a giant; You Fa raised an army and turned against himself—

sentences.zh: 風吹鶂而襄墜兮，神壓紐而平王。

translations.literal: wind blew the osprey and Xiang fell; the divine pressed the cord and King Ping arose—
translations.idiomatic: wind blew the osprey and Xiang fell; the divine pressed the cord and King Ping arose—

sentences.zh: 被嬴縮之由人兮，信吉凶之在己。

translations.literal: suffering Ying Suo's binding came from men— trust that fortune and misfortune lie in oneself—
translations.idiomatic: suffering Ying Suo's binding came from men— trust that fortune and misfortune lie in oneself—

sentences.zh: 或勤憂以減齡兮，亦安樂而獲祉。

translations.literal: some through anxious toil shorten their years; some through ease and joy receive blessings—
translations.idiomatic: some through anxious toil shorten their years; some through ease and joy receive blessings—

sentences.zh: 弟成師而害兄兮，父純臣而烹子。

translations.literal: trusting in spiritual fate to sustain himself, accepting whatever life and destiny bring—
translations.idiomatic: trusting in spiritual fate to sustain himself, accepting whatever life and destiny bring—

sentences.zh: 既聽天而委化兮，無形志之兩疲。

translations.literal: having listened to Heaven and surrendered to transformation, neither form nor will doubly wearied—
translations.idiomatic: having listened to Heaven and surrendered to transformation, neither form nor will doubly wearied—

sentences.zh: 除紛競而靖默兮，守沖寂以無為。

translations.literal: putting aside strife and contention for quiet silence, keeping to empty stillness in non-action—
translations.idiomatic: putting aside strife and contention for quiet silence, keeping to empty stillness in non-action—

sentences.zh: 寄後賢以籍賞兮，寧怨時之弗知。

translations.literal: entrusting later worthies to record and praise, rather than resenting the age for not knowing—
translations.idiomatic: entrusting later worthies to record and praise, rather than resenting the age for not knowing—

sentences.zh: 亂曰：禀元承命，人最靈兮。

translations.literal: Coda: receiving the primal essence and inheriting the mandate, humankind is most spiritual—
translations.idiomatic: Coda: receiving the primal essence and inheriting the mandate, humankind is most spiritual—

sentences.zh: 夭壽否泰，本天成兮。

translations.literal: early death, long life, adversity, prosperity— all are Heaven's completion—
translations.idiomatic: early death, long life, adversity, prosperity— all are Heaven's completion—

sentences.zh: 體源究道，歸聖哲兮。

translations.literal: embodying the source and probing the Way, returning to the sage and wise—
translations.idiomatic: embodying the source and probing the Way, returning to the sage and wise—

sentences.zh: 隨化委遇，能達節兮。

translations.literal: following transformation and accepting encounters, able to grasp the proper measure—
translations.idiomatic: following transformation and accepting encounters, able to grasp the proper measure—

sentences.zh: 顯親揚名，德之上兮。

translations.literal: honoring one's parents and spreading one's name— the highest virtue—
translations.idiomatic: honoring one's parents and spreading one's name— the highest virtue—

sentences.zh: 保家全身，亦厚量兮。

translations.literal: preserving the family and keeping the person whole— also a weighty measure—
translations.idiomatic: preserving the family and keeping the person whole— also a weighty measure—

sentences.zh: 趣世浮動，違性命兮。

translations.literal: chasing the world in restless motion— violating life and nature—
translations.idiomatic: chasing the world in restless motion— violating life and nature—

sentences.zh: 鑒始究終，同水鏡兮。

translations.literal: examining the beginning and probing the end, like water and mirror alike—
translations.idiomatic: examining the beginning and probing the end, like water and mirror alike—

sentences.zh: 志願不合，思遠遊兮。

translations.literal: when aspiration and wish do not accord, one thinks of distant wandering—
translations.idiomatic: when aspiration and wish do not accord, one thinks of distant wandering—

sentences.zh: 陵虛騁志，從所求兮。

translations.literal: crossing the void and unleashing one's will, following what one seeks—
translations.idiomatic: crossing the void and unleashing one's will, following what one seeks—

sentences.zh: 周歷四極，騰八表兮。

translations.literal: circumambulating the four extremities, soaring through the eight directions—
translations.idiomatic: circumambulating the four extremities, soaring through the eight directions—

sentences.zh: 形勞志沮，未衷道兮。

translations.literal: the body weary, the will discouraged— not yet centered in the Way—
translations.idiomatic: the body weary, the will discouraged— not yet centered in the Way—

sentences.zh: 反我遊駕，養慈親兮。

translations.literal: turning back my roaming carriage, nurturing my loving parent—
translations.idiomatic: turning back my roaming carriage, nurturing my loving parent—

sentences.zh: 躬耕練藝，齊至人兮。

translations.literal: personally plowing and refining my arts, equal to the perfected man—
translations.idiomatic: personally plowing and refining my arts, equal to the perfected man—

sentences.zh: 固又作刺讒疾嬖幸詩二首曰：

translations.literal: Gu also composed two poems satirizing slander and denouncing favored minions, which read:
translations.idiomatic: Gu also composed two poems satirizing slander and denouncing favored minions. They read:

sentences.zh: 巧佞！

translations.literal: Crafty flatterer!
translations.idiomatic: Crafty flatterer!

sentences.zh: 巧佞！

translations.literal: Crafty flatterer!
translations.idiomatic: Crafty flatterer!

sentences.zh: [1]讒言興兮。

translations.literal: Slander rises—
translations.idiomatic: Slander rises—

sentences.zh: 營營習習，似青蠅兮。

translations.literal: bustling and swarming, like green flies—
translations.idiomatic: bustling and swarming, like green flies—

sentences.zh: 以白為黑，在汝口兮。

translations.literal: turning white into black, all in your mouth—
translations.idiomatic: turning white into black, all in your mouth—

sentences.zh: 汝非蝮蠆，毒何厚兮。

translations.literal: you are no viper or scorpion— yet how thick your poison—
translations.idiomatic: you are no viper or scorpion— yet how thick your poison—

sentences.zh: 巧佞！

translations.literal: Crafty flatterer!
translations.idiomatic: Crafty flatterer!

sentences.zh: 巧佞！

translations.literal: Crafty flatterer!
translations.idiomatic: Crafty flatterer!

sentences.zh: 一何工矣。

translations.literal: How skilled you are!
translations.idiomatic: How skilled you are!

sentences.zh: 司間司忿，言必從矣。

translations.literal: You watch for gaps and nurse resentment; your words are always obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: You watch for gaps and nurse resentment; your words are always obeyed.

sentences.zh: 朋黨噂𠴲，自相同矣。

translations.literal: Faction and whispered slander— you all match one another.
translations.idiomatic: Faction and whispered slander— you all match one another.

sentences.zh: 浸潤之譖，傾人墉矣。

translations.literal: Steeped slander— it topples a man's wall.
translations.idiomatic: Steeped slander— it topples a man's wall.

sentences.zh: 成人之美，君子貴焉。

translations.literal: To complete another's merit— the gentleman prizes this.
translations.idiomatic: To complete another's merit— the gentleman prizes this.

sentences.zh: [2]攻人之惡，君子耻焉。

translations.literal: To attack another's faults— the gentleman is shamed by this.
translations.idiomatic: To attack another's faults— the gentleman is shamed by this.

sentences.zh: 汝何人斯？

translations.literal: What sort of person are you?
translations.idiomatic: What sort of person are you?

sentences.zh: 譖毀日繁。

translations.literal: Slander and defamation grow daily.
translations.idiomatic: Slander and defamation grow daily.

sentences.zh: 予實無罪，騁汝詭言。

translations.literal: I am truly without guilt, yet you unleash your deceitful words.
translations.idiomatic: I am truly without guilt, yet you unleash your deceitful words.

sentences.zh: 番番緝緝，讒言側入。

translations.literal: Again and again, slyly and stealthily, slander slips in from the side.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again, slyly and stealthily, slander slips in from the side.

sentences.zh: 君子好讒，如或弗及。

translations.literal: The gentleman loves slander as if he could not get enough.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman loves slander as if he could not get enough.

sentences.zh: 天疾讒說，汝其至矣。

translations.literal: Heaven hates slanderous speech— you have reached your limit.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven hates slanderous speech— you have reached your limit.

sentences.zh: 無妄之禍，行將及矣。

translations.literal: Undeserved calamity is about to overtake you.
translations.idiomatic: Undeserved calamity is about to overtake you.

sentences.zh: 泛泛遊鳧，弗制弗拘。

translations.literal: The duck drifts freely, unbridled, unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: The duck drifts freely, unbridled, unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 行藏之徒，或智或愚。

translations.literal: Among those who act or withdraw, some are wise and some foolish.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who act or withdraw, some are wise and some foolish.

sentences.zh: 維予小人，未明茲理。

translations.literal: I, a petty man, have not yet understood this principle.
translations.idiomatic: I, a petty man, have not yet understood this principle.

sentences.zh: 毀與行俱，言與釁起。

translations.literal: Slander goes with conduct; words arise with cause for offense.
translations.idiomatic: Slander goes with conduct; words arise with cause for offense.

sentences.zh: 我其懲矣，我其悔矣。

translations.literal: I shall take warning; I shall repent.
translations.idiomatic: I shall take warning; I shall repent.

sentences.zh: 豈求人兮，忠恕在己。

translations.literal: How could one seek it in others? Loyalty and forbearance lie in oneself.
translations.idiomatic: How could one seek it in others? Loyalty and forbearance lie in oneself.

sentences.zh: 彼諂諛兮，人之蠹兮。

translations.literal: Those flatterers— the vermin of mankind—
translations.idiomatic: Those flatterers— the vermin of mankind—

sentences.zh: 剌促昔粟，罔顧耻辱，以求媚兮。

translations.literal: Hurrying and scheming, heedless of shame, to win favor—
translations.idiomatic: Hurrying and scheming, heedless of shame, to win favor—

sentences.zh: 邪干側入，如恐弗及，以自容兮。

translations.literal: Approaching by crooked paths from the side, as if fearing not to arrive, to secure themselves—
translations.idiomatic: Approaching by crooked paths from the side, as if fearing not to arrive, to secure themselves—

sentences.zh: 志行褊小，好習不道。

translations.literal: Their will and conduct are narrow and small; they love what is not the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Their will and conduct are narrow and small; they love what is not the Way.

sentences.zh: 朝挾其車，夕承其輿。

translations.literal: Morning they ride in his carriage, evening they attend his litter.
translations.idiomatic: Morning they ride in his carriage, evening they attend his litter.

sentences.zh: 或騎或徒，載奔載趨。

translations.literal: Some on horseback, some on foot, now running, now hurrying.
translations.idiomatic: Some on horseback, some on foot, now running, now hurrying.

sentences.zh: 或言或笑，曲事親要。

translations.literal: Now speaking, now laughing, they twist affairs to please the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Now speaking, now laughing, they twist affairs to please the powerful.

sentences.zh: 正路不由，邪徑是蹈。

translations.literal: They do not follow the straight road; they tread the crooked path.
translations.idiomatic: They do not follow the straight road; they tread the crooked path.

sentences.zh: 不識大猷，不知話言。

translations.literal: They do not know the great plan; they do not understand proper speech.
translations.idiomatic: They do not know the great plan; they do not understand proper speech.

sentences.zh: 其朋其黨，其徒實繁。

translations.literal: Their factions and cliques, their followers, are truly numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Their factions and cliques, their followers, are truly numerous.

sentences.zh: 有詭其行，有佞其音。

translations.literal: Some deceive in conduct, some flatter in voice.
translations.idiomatic: Some deceive in conduct, some flatter in voice.

sentences.zh: 蘧蒢戚施，邪媚是欽。

translations.literal: Bent-backed and hunch-shouldered, they revere crooked flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Bent-backed and hunch-shouldered, they revere crooked flattery.

sentences.zh: 既詭且妬，以逞其心。

translations.literal: Both deceitful and jealous, to give full vent to their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Both deceitful and jealous, to give full vent to their hearts.

sentences.zh: 是信是任，敗其以多。

translations.literal: Trusted and employed, they ruin many through it.
translations.idiomatic: Trusted and employed, they ruin many through it.

sentences.zh: 不始不慎，末如之何。

translations.literal: If one is not careful at the start, at the end nothing can be done.
translations.idiomatic: If one is not careful at the start, at the end nothing can be done.

sentences.zh: 習習宰嚭，營營無極。

translations.literal: Busy, busy, like Zai Pi, scheming without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Busy, busy, like Zai Pi, scheming without limit.

sentences.zh: 梁丘寡智，王鮒淺識。

translations.literal: Liang Qiu lacked wisdom; Wang Fu had shallow understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qiu lacked wisdom; Wang Fu had shallow understanding.

sentences.zh: 伊戾、息夫，異世同力。

translations.literal: Yi Li and Xi Fu, in different ages, exerted the same power.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Li and Xi Fu, in different ages, exerted the same power.

sentences.zh: 江充、趙高，甘言似直。

translations.literal: Jiang Chong and Zhao Gao— sweet words that seem straight.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Chong and Zhao Gao— sweet words that seem straight.

sentences.zh: 豎刁、上官，擅生羽翼。

translations.literal: Shu Diao and Shangguan— they grew wings of their own.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Diao and Shangguan— they grew wings of their own.

sentences.zh: 乃如之人，僭爽其德。

translations.literal: Men like these violate and corrupt their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Men like these violate and corrupt their virtue.

sentences.zh: 豈徒喪邦，又亦覆國。

translations.literal: Not only do they destroy a state— they also overturn a realm.
translations.idiomatic: Not only do they destroy a state— they also overturn a realm.

sentences.zh: 嗟爾中下，其親其昵。

translations.literal: Alas, you middling and lowly men, so close and so intimate—
translations.idiomatic: Alas, you middling and lowly men, so close and so intimate—

sentences.zh: 不謂其非，不覺其失。

translations.literal: You do not call their conduct wrong; you do not perceive their faults.
translations.idiomatic: You do not call their conduct wrong; you do not perceive their faults.

sentences.zh: 好之有年，寵之有日。

translations.literal: You have favored them for years; you have pampered them for days.
translations.idiomatic: You have favored them for years; you have pampered them for days.

sentences.zh: 我思古人，心焉若疾。

translations.literal: When I think of the ancients, my heart is like a sickness.
translations.idiomatic: When I think of the ancients, my heart is like a sickness.

sentences.zh: 凡百君子，宜其慎矣。

translations.literal: All you gentlemen— you should be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: All you gentlemen— you should be cautious.

sentences.zh: 覆車之鑒，近可信矣。

translations.literal: The overturned cart's mirror is near and can be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: The overturned cart's mirror is near and can be trusted.

sentences.zh: 言既備矣，事既至矣。

translations.literal: The words are complete; the matter has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The words are complete; the matter has arrived.

sentences.zh: 反是不思，維塵及矣。

translations.literal: If you do not turn from this, only dust will reach you.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not turn from this, only dust will reach you.

sentences.zh: 神龜末，清河王懌領太尉，辟固從事中郎。

translations.literal: Near the end of the Shengui era, Prince of Qinghe Yi served as Grand Commandant and summoned Gu as Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Shengui era, Prince Yi of Qinghe served as Grand Commandant and summoned Gu as Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 屬懌被害，元叉秉政，朝野震悚。

translations.literal: When Yi was killed, Yuan Cha seized power, and court and countryside were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was killed, Yuan Cha seized power, and court and countryside were shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 懌諸子及門生吏僚莫不慮禍，隱避不出，素為懌所厚者彌不自安。

translations.literal: Yi's sons, retainers, and clerks all feared calamity and hid without emerging; those Yi had treated generously were especially ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's sons, retainers, and clerks all feared calamity and hid without emerging; those Yi had treated generously were especially ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 固以嘗被辟命，遂獨詣喪所，盡哀慟哭，良久乃還。

translations.literal: Gu, having once received Yi's summons, thereupon went alone to the mourning hall, weeping in full grief for a long time before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Gu, having once received Yi's summons, thereupon went alone to the mourning hall, weeping in full grief for a long time before returning.

sentences.zh: 僕射游肇聞而歎曰：「雖欒布、王脩何以尚也，君子哉若人！

translations.literal: Vice Director You Zhao heard of it and sighed: "Even Luan Bu and Wang Xiu could not surpass this— what a gentleman this man is!
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director You Zhao heard of it and sighed: "Even Luan Bu and Wang Xiu could not surpass this— what a gentleman this man is!

sentences.zh: 」及汝南王悅為太尉，選舉多非其人，又輕肆檛撻，固以前為元卿，雖離國，猶上疏切諫。

translations.literal: When Prince of Runan Yue became Grand Commandant, his selections were mostly unworthy men, and he lightly and recklessly beat people with whips. Gu, because he had formerly served as Attendant Gentleman under the Prince of Qinghe, though now separated from the princely establishment, still submitted a memorial of sharp remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yue of Runan became Grand Commandant, his selections were mostly unworthy men, and he lightly and recklessly beat people with whips. Gu, because he had formerly served as Attendant Gentleman under the Prince of Qinghe, though now separated from the princely establishment, still submitted a memorial of sharp remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 事在悅傳。

translations.literal: The account is in Yue's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The account is in Yue's biography.

sentences.zh: 悅辟固為從事中郎，不就。

translations.literal: Yue summoned Gu as Attendant Gentleman, but Gu did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yue summoned Gu as Attendant Gentleman, but Gu did not accept.

sentences.zh: 正光二年，京兆王繼為司徒，高選官僚，辟固從事中郎，加鎮遠將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengguang, Prince of Jingzhao Ji served as Minister of Works and made high selections among officials; he summoned Gu as Attendant Gentleman and additionally appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengguang, Prince Ji of Jingzhao served as Minister of Works and made high selections among officials; he summoned Gu as Attendant Gentleman and additionally appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 府解，除前軍將軍，鎮遠如故。

translations.literal: When the headquarters was dissolved, he was appointed General of the Vanguard, retaining his title as General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: When the headquarters was dissolved, he was appointed General of the Vanguard, retaining his title as General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 又典科揚州勳賞。

translations.literal: He also supervised the assessment and rewards of meritorious service in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also supervised the assessment and rewards of meritorious service in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初硤石之役，固有先登之功，而朝賞未及，至是與尚書令李崇訟勳更表。

translations.literal: In the initial Battle of Xiashi, Gu had merit for being first to ascend the walls, but court rewards had not yet reached him; at this time he joined Minister of Works Li Chong in memorializing to dispute the merit records.
translations.idiomatic: In the initial Battle of Xiashi, Gu had merit for being first to ascend the walls, but court rewards had not yet reached him; at this time he joined Minister of Works Li Chong in memorializing to dispute the merit records.

sentences.zh: 崇雖貴盛，固據理不撓，談者稱焉。

translations.literal: Though Li Chong was noble and powerful, Gu held to reason without yielding; commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Li Chong was noble and powerful, Gu held to reason without yielding; commentators praised him.

sentences.zh: 四年九月卒，時年五十七。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year he died, at the age of fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year he died, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈輔國將軍、太常少卿，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded General Who Assists the State and Vice Minister of Ceremonies, with the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded General Who Assists the State and Vice Minister of Ceremonies, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 固剛直雅正，不畏強禦，居官清潔，家無餘財，終歿之日，室徒四壁，無以供喪，親故為其棺斂焉。

translations.literal: Gu was upright, refined, and correct, unafraid of the powerful; in office he was clean, and his household had no surplus wealth. On the day he died, his rooms had only four bare walls, with nothing to supply the funeral; relatives and friends provided his coffin and shroud.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was upright, refined, and correct, unafraid of the powerful; in office he was clean, and his household had no surplus wealth. On the day he died, his rooms had only four bare walls, with nothing to supply the funeral; relatives and friends provided his coffin and shroud.

sentences.zh: 初，固著終制一篇，[3]務從儉約。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gu had composed a chapter on funeral regulations, [3] striving for thrift and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gu had composed a chapter on funeral regulations, [3] striving for thrift and simplicity.

sentences.zh: 臨終，又敕諸子一遵先制。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he again ordered his sons to follow the earlier regulations in full.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he again ordered his sons to follow the earlier regulations in full.

sentences.zh: 固有三子。

translations.literal: Gu had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Gu had three sons.

translations.literal: [4] The Northern History, juan 47, reads "five sons" for "three sons".
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note: The Northern History, juan 47, reads "five sons" for "three sons" here.

sentences.zh: 長休之，武定末，黃門郎。

translations.literal: The eldest, Xiuzhi, at the end of the Wuding era served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Xiuzhi, at the end of the Wuding era served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 休之弟詮之，字子衡。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's younger brother Quanzhi, styled Ziheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's younger brother Quanzhi, styled Ziheng.

sentences.zh: 少著才名，辟司徒行參軍。

translations.literal: From youth he showed literary talent and was summoned as Acting Staff Officer in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed literary talent and was summoned as Acting Staff Officer in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 早為門生所害，時人悼惜之。

translations.literal: He was killed early by a retainer; people of the time mourned and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed early by a retainer; people of the time mourned and regretted it.

sentences.zh: 賈思伯，字士休，齊郡益都人也。

translations.literal: Jia Sibo, styled Shixiu, was a native of Yidu in Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sibo, styled Shixiu, was a native of Yidu in Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 世父元壽，高祖時中書侍郎，有學行，見稱於時。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Yuanshou, during the reign of Emperor Gaozu, served as Attendant Gentleman in the Palace Library and possessed learning and conduct, being praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Yuanshou, during the reign of Emperor Gaozu, served as Attendant Gentleman in the Palace Library and possessed learning and conduct, being praised in his time.

sentences.zh: 思伯釋褐奉朝請，太子步兵校尉、中書舍人，轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Sibo began his career as Attendant at Court, Captain of the Footmen of the Heir Apparent and Palace Library Attendant, then was transferred to Attendant Gentleman in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Sibo began his career as Attendant at Court, Captain of the Footmen of the Heir Apparent and Palace Library Attendant, then was transferred to Attendant Gentleman in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 頗為高祖所知，常從征伐。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu came to know him well, and he often followed on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu came to know him well, and he often followed on campaigns.

sentences.zh: 及世宗即位，以侍從之勤，轉輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, on account of his diligence as an attendant he was transferred to General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu acceded, on account of his diligence as an attendant he was transferred to General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 任城王澄之圍鍾離也，以思伯持節為其軍司。

translations.literal: When Prince of Rencheng Cheng besieged Zhongli, Sibo held the staff of authority as Army Supervisor for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Cheng of Rencheng besieged Zhongli, Sibo held the staff of authority as Army Supervisor for him.

sentences.zh: 及澄失利，思伯為後殿。

translations.literal: When Cheng suffered defeat, Sibo served as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng suffered defeat, Sibo served as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 澄以思伯儒者，謂之必死。

translations.literal: Cheng, because Sibo was a Confucian scholar, thought he would surely die.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, because Sibo was a Confucian scholar, thought he would surely die.

sentences.zh: 及至，大喜，曰：「仁者必有勇，常謂虛談，今於軍司見之矣。

translations.literal: When Sibo arrived, Cheng was greatly pleased and said: "The benevolent must have courage— I always thought that empty talk, but now I see it in the Army Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: When Sibo arrived, Cheng was greatly pleased and said: "The benevolent must have courage— I always thought that empty talk, but now I see it in the Army Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 」思伯託以失道，不伐其功，時論稱其長者。

translations.literal: Sibo pleaded that he had lost his way and did not boast of his merit; commentators of the time praised him as a man of mature character.
translations.idiomatic: Sibo pleaded that he had lost his way and did not boast of his merit; commentators of the time praised him as a man of mature character.

sentences.zh: 後為河內太守，不拜。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Administrator of Henei but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Administrator of Henei but did not accept.

sentences.zh: 尋除鴻臚少卿，以母憂免。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and was removed on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and was removed on account of mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，徵為滎陽太守，有政績。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned as Administrator of Xingyang and had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was summoned as Administrator of Xingyang and had administrative achievements.

sentences.zh: 遷征虜將軍、南青州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Inspector of Southern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Inspector of Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，思伯與弟思同師事北海陰鳳授業，無資酬之，鳳遂質其衣物。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sibo and his younger brother Sitong had studied under Yin Feng of Beihai; having no means to pay him, Feng thereupon pawned their clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Sibo and his younger brother Sitong had studied under Yin Feng of Beihai; having no means to pay him, Feng thereupon pawned their clothing.

sentences.zh: 及思伯之部，送縑百匹遺鳳，因具車馬迎之，鳳慚不往。

translations.literal: When Sibo reached his post, he sent a hundred bolts of silk to Feng and prepared carriage and horses to welcome him; Feng was ashamed and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Sibo reached his post, he sent a hundred bolts of silk to Feng and prepared carriage and horses to welcome him; Feng was ashamed and did not go.

sentences.zh: 時人稱嘆焉。

translations.literal: People of the time praised and admired this.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time praised and admired this.

sentences.zh: 尋以父憂免。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was removed on account of mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was removed on account of mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 後除征虜將軍、光祿少卿，仍拜左將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Splendor, and was again appointed General of the Left and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Splendor, and was again appointed General of the Left and Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，徵為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Suzong he was summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat in the Affairs Section.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Xiaoming he was summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat in the Affairs Section.

sentences.zh: 因請拜掃，還鄉里。

translations.literal: He thereupon requested leave to sweep the tombs and return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon requested leave to sweep the tombs and return to his home district.

sentences.zh: 未拜，以風聞免。

translations.literal: Before he could accept appointment, he was removed on account of adverse reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could accept appointment, he was removed on account of adverse reputation.

sentences.zh: 尋除右將軍、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed General of the Right and Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed General of the Right and Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 思伯以州邊遠，不樂外出，辭以男女未婚。

translations.literal: Sibo, because the province was remote on the frontier, was unwilling to go far away and declined on the grounds that his sons and daughters were not yet married.
translations.idiomatic: Sibo, because the province was remote on the frontier, was unwilling to go far away and declined on the grounds that his sons and daughters were not yet married.

sentences.zh: 靈太后不許，舍人徐紇言之，得改授太尉長史。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling would not permit it; Attendant Xu Zhi spoke on his behalf, and he was reassigned as Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling would not permit it; Attendant Xu Zhi spoke on his behalf, and he was reassigned as Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 又除安東將軍、廷尉卿。

translations.literal: He was again appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 思伯自以儒素為業，不好法律，希言事。

translations.literal: Sibo considered Confucian learning his vocation and did not love the law; he rarely spoke of legal matters.
translations.idiomatic: Sibo considered Confucian learning his vocation and did not love the law; he rarely spoke of legal matters.

sentences.zh: 俄轉衞尉卿。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Director of the Court of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to Director of the Court of the Imperial Guard.
